coordinates.note: No official DOE/WIPP page or technical/geodetic paper fetched in this session states coordinates; this is the site's general campus/surface location per Wikipedia only (rank 12, pointer), used here per the ontology's rule that geocoder/Wikipedia coordinates are acceptable ONLY for kind: campus|headquarters, labelled approximate. EXO-200's own underground placement (~655 m below this surface point) is recorded on the detector's placement note rather than as a separate `detector`-kind coordinate, since no rank<=7 source gives an underground coordinate distinct from this campus point.

depth.note: Converted from the quoted feet figure (2,150 ft x 0.3048 = 655.3 m).
depth.quote: Transuranic waste is disposed of 2,150 feet underground in rooms mined from the salt bed.

depth_mwe.locator: The EXO-200 detector, part I: Detector design and construction (arXiv:1202.2192), site description
depth_mwe.note: Verification fix (2026-09-17): this agent directly fetched the EXO-200 detector design paper, which gives this figure; a later EXO-200 paper (Searches for Double Beta Decay of 134Xe with EXO-200) instead reports ~1624 (+22/-21) m.w.e. for the underground clean room, a later re-estimate not independently re-verified against a directly fetched primary source in this session. The construction paper's 1585 m.w.e. figure is recorded here as the directly sourced value; the discrepancy with the later 1624 m.w.e. figure is noted for a future pass.
depth_mwe.quote: EXO-200 is located at a depth of 1585 m water equivalent ... in the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (WIPP) near Carlsbad, New Mexico

name: WIPP surface campus, Carlsbad, New Mexico
notes: This is a campus-level approximate marker (Wikipedia-sourced), not a detector-kind coordinate; per the coordinate rules (and v0.2 A23), EXO-200's underground hall/clean-room position is unsourced in this session and is not relabelled as `detector`/`underground_lab`.

summary.plain: A patch of New Mexico desert above a deep salt mine. The mine below stores nuclear waste, and from 2011 to 2018 also housed the EXO-200 neutrino experiment.
summary.technical: Surface campus of WIPP near Carlsbad, New Mexico; underground rooms ~655 m below in a Permian salt bed hosted the EXO-200 136Xe TPC 2011-2018.
